name: Patent Agent
title: Patent Agent & Patent Attorney
intro: From Class 12 Science to a registered patent agent: a science, engineering or technology degree, patent-law preparation, the Patent Agent Examination (Paper I and II), registration at 21+, and optionally an LLB to become a patent attorney.

phases.title: Class 12 Science
phases.summary: PCM or PCB — the degree must be in science, engineering or technology.
points: The degree must be in science, engineering or technology, so Class 12 Science is the practical route.
B.Com or BA graduates cannot become patent agents.
You must be an Indian citizen.

phases.title: Science / engineering / tech degree
phases.summary: Pharma, biotech, electronics and computer science are in high demand.
points: A degree in science, engineering or technology from a recognised university, or an equivalent the Government specifies.
Pharma, biotech, electronics and computer-science backgrounds are in high demand.
Patent search and analytics roles are a common first job.

phases.title: Prepare patent law
phases.summary: The Patents Act, 1970 and Patents Rules — drafting practice matters most.
points: Study the Patents Act, 1970 and the Patents Rules.
Practise drafting specifications and claims, and interpreting patent documents.
Section 126 of the Patents Act sets out who may register.

phases.title: Patent Agent Examination
phases.summary: Paper I (objective) and Paper II (descriptive), per the current notice.
points: Paper I: objective, multiple-choice questions on the Patents Act and Rules.
Paper II: descriptive — drafting specifications and claims, and interpreting patent documents.
Minimum marks per paper and any viva are fixed in each year's notice from the CGPDTM (IP India).

phases.title: Register and practise
phases.summary: Register, then join an IP firm, a company IP cell or start your own practice.
points: You must be at least 21; apply for registration with the required documents (including your degree) within the time the result notice allows.
Employers: IP law firms, pharma and tech companies' IP cells, patent analytics firms, university tech-transfer offices; growth: analyst → agent → senior associate → partner / head of IP.
Optional: an LLB makes you a patent attorney who can also argue cases in court; the Patent Office recruits Examiners through its own exam.
